boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Michigan Tech traditions spanning the academic year, from Keweenaw Day to Winter Carnival snow statues.

cards.title: An Afternoon on the Town
cards.subtitle: Campus, downtown Houghton, and Hancock
cards.notes: Start on campus, then follow the participating stops through Houghton and Hancock for the university-sponsored welcome event.
cards.short_summary: A campus-to-downtown welcome event connecting students with local businesses and services.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech lists An Afternoon on the Town as an event that begins on campus and extends through downtown Houghton and Hancock.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current university event details for participating locations and timing.

cards.title: Welcome Week
cards.subtitle: Michigan Technological University campus
cards.notes: Use the week’s official schedule to sample social activities, entertainment, and campus updates as the academic year starts.
cards.short_summary: A week-long return-to-campus tradition for new and returning Michigan Tech students.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech identifies Welcome Week as an annual, week-long tradition designed to welcome students back to campus.
cards.access_notes: Dates and activities vary by year; use the university’s current schedule.

cards.title: K-Day
cards.subtitle: Chassell Centennial Park, Chassell
cards.notes: Visit the registered-student-organization fair to meet campus groups; classes release at noon on the Friday of Labor Day week.
cards.short_summary: Keweenaw Day combines an organization fair with an early release for the Michigan Tech community.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech calls K-Day an annual tradition held on the Friday of Labor Day week and a fair with around 200 registered student groups.
cards.access_notes: The university lists the 2026 event for September 11, 1–5 p.m., at Chassell Centennial Park.

cards.title: Festival of Nations
cards.subtitle: Dee Stadium and Houghton waterfront
cards.notes: See the international displays and entertainment around Dee Stadium; this 2026 event continues elements of the former Parade of Nations.
cards.short_summary: A new multicultural festival format carrying forward staples of Michigan Tech’s former Parade of Nations.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech describes Festival of Nations as a 2026 successor to the former Parade of Nations, expanding activities from Dee Stadium toward the waterfront pier.
cards.access_notes: Michigan Tech lists the inaugural Festival of Nations for September 19, 2026, noon–4 p.m.

cards.title: Race Cardboard Boats at Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Keweenaw Waterway, Houghton
cards.notes: Watch or join the Homecoming cardboard-boat-race programming on the Keweenaw Waterway, alongside the broader Husky Spirit celebration.
cards.short_summary: Cardboard boat races are a named Michigan Tech Homecoming activity on the Keweenaw Waterway.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech states that its Homecoming includes cardboard boat races on the Keweenaw Waterway.
cards.access_notes: Check current Homecoming programming for participation and viewing details.

cards.title: Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: Michigan Technological University and the Keweenaw
cards.notes: Plan a fall visit around arts and athletic events, then leave time to explore campus and the Keweenaw with visiting family.
cards.short_summary: A fall tradition for families to reconnect with their Husky and experience campus and the Keweenaw.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech describes Family Weekend as a fall-semester opportunity for families to reconnect, attend events, and explore the area.
cards.access_notes: Michigan Tech places the event in late September or early October; consult the annual schedule.

cards.title: Winter Carnival Since 1922
cards.subtitle: Michigan Technological University and Houghton
cards.notes: Visit in early February to see the campus-wide winter festival and its student-built works, games, and scheduled performances.
cards.short_summary: Michigan Tech’s signature early-February winter festival began as an Ice Carnival in 1922.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech says Winter Carnival began in 1922 and has been organized by Blue Key National Honor Society since 1934.
cards.access_notes: The university lists the next Winter Carnival dates as February 3–6, 2027.

cards.title: Build a Winter Carnival Snow Statue
cards.subtitle: Michigan Tech campus and surrounding community
cards.notes: Find the statue sites during Carnival and follow the published rules if participating; some teams build in month-long and all-night categories.
cards.short_summary: Large snow sculptures are a defining Winter Carnival practice, judged in distinct construction categories.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech reports that Winter Carnival snow statues are judged in month-long and all-night categories and calls them an iconic part of the celebration.
cards.access_notes: Use the annual Winter Carnival materials for statue locations, rules, and participation details.

cards.title: Broomball in Winter
cards.subtitle: Michigan Technological University
cards.notes: Follow the intramural schedule or rink cam to catch a game; broomball is one of the winter traditions introduced during Welcome Week.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale winter broomball culture with more than 200 teams and over 1,000 games.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech identifies broomball as a campus tradition and says more than 200 teams play more than 1,000 games each winter.
cards.access_notes: Check current recreation or Winter Carnival information for schedules and participation requirements.

cards.title: Spring Fling
cards.subtitle: Michigan Technological University campus
cards.notes: Look for the mid-April campus carnival schedule and choose among its food, games, and live-entertainment activities.
cards.short_summary: A mid-April campus-wide carnival marking the return of warmer weather.
cards.evidence_claim: Michigan Tech describes Spring Fling as a mid-April campus-wide carnival with food, games, and live entertainment.
cards.access_notes: Dates and activity details vary annually; consult the university’s current event schedule.
